events.title: Map Milk Bar research coverage and remaining evidence gaps
events.summary: The reusable assessment distinguishes customer occasions, cup/flight scenarios and less-developed take-home or delivery models. No format has demonstrated paid repeat demand in the reviewed records.
events.why: A complete research document can still depend on assumed demand, operating terms and labor. The next commitment needs the relevant gaps visible.
events.revisitWhen: A chosen offer, new buyer evidence, supplier/site terms or measured performance changes the assessment.

sources.label: Milk Bar coverage and evidence gaps

events.title: Map Oats research coverage and remaining evidence gaps
events.summary: The assessment records existing desk research and scenario models alongside missing buyer selection, complete service economics, operating determinations and paid test results.
events.why: Selecting a buyer and occasion gives the pricing, acquisition and delivery model a consistent transaction to assess.
events.revisitWhen: Actual buyer requirements, costs, operating timing or test evidence changes the decision.

events.title: Explore milk tastings alongside prepared specialty drinks
events.summary: The working concept combines simple milk-forward offerings, discovery flights and signature drinks. These remain concepts, not validated products.
events.why: The two experiences could appeal to different purchase occasions; neither customer appeal has yet been proven.
events.revisitWhen: Customer interviews and paid tests show which offer people actually buy and return for.

sources.label: Milk Bar concept and decision record

events.title: Explore a quick-service counter with a small tasting area
events.summary: An express order-and-pickup flow and a two-to-four-person standing tasting ledge are the preferred experience to investigate.
events.why: A small tasting area might support discovery while keeping regular orders fast, but layout, permissions and economics remain unverified.
events.revisitWhen: Regulatory requirements, site dimensions or observed queue times make the format impractical.

sources.label: Milk Bar experience and open constraints

events.title: Test discovery and repeat-drink appeals before selecting a lead
events.summary: Compare willingness to purchase a tasting flight with willingness to buy a favorite milk-centered drink repeatedly.
events.why: Preference expressed in brainstorming is not evidence of price acceptance or repeat demand.
events.revisitWhen: A defined research sample and actual purchases support a clear lead offer.

sources.label: Milk Bar hypotheses and recorded choices

events.title: No external market validation was recorded at archive time
events.summary: The repository contained a concept and a research brief, but no completed field research, sales or verified unit economics.
events.why: The archive must distinguish research intentions from completed research and observed customer behavior.
events.revisitWhen: Dated, source-backed research or real demand-test results are committed.

events.title: Explore fudge as a sharing or gifting purchase
events.summary: Sharing occasions, gift-ready packaging and an everyday treat are concept directions under consideration, not a chosen product line.
events.why: The buying occasion may matter as much as the flavor, but customer purchase behavior has not yet selected a direction.
events.revisitWhen: Interviews and a priced offer reveal which occasion attracts paid orders.

events.title: Consider a small paid preorder gift-box pilot
events.summary: The research proposes a limited batch of up to twenty 8-ounce boxes with predeclared order, cost and owner-hour thresholds; no launch was approved.
events.why: A paid pilot would test demand and economics more directly than compliments, free samples or visual concepts.
events.revisitWhen: Production requirements and owner budget are confirmed, then the experiment is explicitly approved or rejected.

sources.label: Fudge pilot proposal and decision gates

events.title: Keep name, recipes, production method and prices undecided
events.summary: The proposed business has not settled its brand, recipe, sale price, capital budget or homemade-versus-partner production model.
events.why: Customer demand, legal requirements and genuine cost estimates should guide commitments.
events.revisitWhen: Source-backed estimates and owner choices resolve these constraints.

events.title: Use Oats, Etc. as a working name
events.summary: The brand direction moved away from Oats & More after a potentially conflicting cereal trademark was identified. Legal clearance is not established.
events.why: The prior name posed potential naming risk; a new URL or attractive name is not proof of trademark availability.
events.revisitWhen: Official and common-law trademark checks establish whether the working name can be used.

events.title: Start with a narrow oatmeal breakfast pilot
events.summary: The current pilot direction focuses on familiar oatmeal and simple toppings; the earlier broader sweet-and-savory breakfast/lunch concept remains a possible later stage.
events.why: A smaller initial menu can reduce preparation, equipment and marketing complexity during validation.
events.revisitWhen: Real customer demand and measured operating capacity justify testing additional products or dayparts.

sources.label: Oats research overview and operating principles

events.title: Defer major cart or trailer purchases until demand and site are verified
events.summary: An approved recurring location, electrical access, safe operating model and paying customers should come before buying specialized equipment.
events.why: The hosted-site approach weakens the case for an e-bike, while towing limits and fully loaded weight complicate a trailer.
events.revisitWhen: A specific compliant site, actual demand and measured equipment needs justify a purchase.

events.title: Thirty bowls before 9 a.m. is a capacity target, not demand evidence
events.summary: The proposed first test aims at thirty servings before 9 a.m.; actual host traffic, conversion, portion yield and one-person throughput remain unknown.
events.why: A volume target alone cannot establish either the size of the market or profitability.
events.revisitWhen: A permitted test measures actual orders, demand denominator, serving times, waste and contribution.

events.title: Treat anonymous flavor votes as directional feedback only
events.summary: The existing Cloudflare poll measures browser-based preference, not verified unique buyers or willingness to pay.
events.why: Repeat browsers, self-selection and free-choice behavior prevent vote totals from forecasting paid sales.
events.revisitWhen: A priced offer and repeat purchases provide stronger demand evidence.

events.title: Validate a host site and real breakfast demand before purchasing
events.summary: Seek an office host, clarify food-service and property permissions, then test actual paid demand at a specified price.
events.why: The host and the breakfast customer are separate necessary gates; neither has been validated by the published poll.
events.revisitWhen: A specific location agrees to the proposed arrangement and paid testing yields measured results.
